title: The lights and beeps on a vehicle
summary: The lights on a vehicle in R.E.P.O. are part of the machine rather than decoration: a front and a back light each have their own renderer and emission colour, they flicker with a minimum time on, reversing can beep on an interval, the boost has a light with a curve, and a hover effect can be scrolled, rotated and scaled.
body: A vehicle's lights are wired into the vehicle rather than left to the model. There is a front light and a back light, and each has its own renderer and its own emission colour, which is why one can be dimmed or coloured differently from the other.
They flicker. There is a duration for the flicker and a minimum time a light stays on, so a failing or strobing light is a pair of settings rather than an animation baked into the object.
The vehicle can announce that it is reversing. Backing up can be given beeps with an interval of its own, which is why a reversing vehicle can be heard before it is seen.
The boost has a light of its own. There is a boost light with a curve and a duration, so using the boost is marked on the vehicle rather than only on the speedometer.

A vehicle can also hover, and the effect is drawn rather than simulated. There are renderers for the whole effect and for its front and back, so a hover can be drawn around the vehicle and not only under it.

That effect moves. There is a scroll speed, a noise speed and a noise strength for the scroll, rotation speeds for two axes with their own noise, and a scaling noise with a speed and a strength, which is why the surface shimmers rather than sliding uniformly.
It can also be offset per mesh, so the same effect lines up differently on different parts of the body rather than being one flat sheet over everything.
There is a mesh set aside for grabbing the vehicle, which is how handling one works when it is not being driven.
What this entry does not tell you: how bright any light is, how often a flicker happens, or how loud a reversing beep is. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: There is a front and a back light, each with its own renderer and emission colour.
facts.evidence: identifiers: frontLight, frontLightRenderer, frontLightEmissionColor, backLight, backLightRenderer, backLightEmissionColor

facts.claim: The lights have a flicker duration and a minimum time they stay on.
Reversing can beep on an interval of its own.
The boost has a light with a curve and a duration.
A hover effect is drawn whole and for its front and back separately.
The hover effect scrolls and rotates with noise, and scales with noise, each with a speed and a strength.
facts.evidence: identifiers: hoverEffectScrollSpeed, hoverEffectScrollNoiseSpeed, hoverEffectScrollNoiseStrength, hoverEffectRotateSpeedX, hoverEffectRotateSpeedZ, hoverEffectRotateNoiseSpeed, hoverEffectRotateNoiseStrength, hoverEffectScaleNoiseSpeed, hoverEffectScaleNoiseStrength

facts.claim: The effect can be offset per mesh.
There is a mesh set aside for grabbing the vehicle.
